titulo: Έχετε — and then whatever you need
subtitulo: Four counters in the first hour, and every one of them answers the same three-word opening
cena: Athens arrivals: the belt has stopped, the phone has not found a network, and there are four counters between you and being able to sit down.
frasePiso: Έχετε, plus the thing. One frame, and the whole arrivals hall becomes answerable.

clique.desconto: Nobody handed you a different sentence for each of those counters. You kept one opening and changed only the thing that came after it.
clique.piso: Next time you need something and do not know whether the place stocks it, you will not mime it. You will ask in three words.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: In Greece the duty is to ACCEPT card payment, not merely to own a terminal. Article 65 of ν.4446/2016, «Υποχρέωση αποδοχής μέσων πληρωμής με κάρτα», imposes it by ΚΑΔ — the trade's activity code — and article 66 obliges the trader to inform the customer visibly at the entrance and at the till. The list of ΚΑΔ was replaced by ΚΥΑ 119899/2023, ΦΕΚ Β΄7115/18.12.2023, which extended it to a further 35 codes including street markets, food retail and kiosks. The honest limit: the legal criterion remains the ΚΑΔ list rather than «all commerce», so universal coverage is contested. IRIS, obligatory across commerce since 01.11.2025, is a domestic instant-payment system that a foreign visitor normally cannot use — what protects the traveller is the card obligation.
fatosDatados.fonte: Aceitar cartão — e a obrigação é de ACEITAR, não só de ter POS. Art. 65 do ν.4446/2016, «Υποχρέωση αποδοχής μέσων πληρωμής με κάρτα», obriga por ΚΑΔ (código de atividade); o art. 66 obriga a informar o consumidor de forma visível na entrada e no caixa. A lista de ΚΑΔ foi substituída pela ΚΥΑ 119899/2023, ΦΕΚ Β΄7115/18.12.2023, que estendeu a mais 35 ΚΑΔ — feiras livres, varejo alimentar, bancas. Duas ressalvas honestas: IRIS é doméstico e o turista estrangeiro normalmente não consegue usar — o que protege o aluno é a obrigação de cartão; e ⚠️ a cobertura NÃO é universal: o critério legal continua sendo a lista de ΚΑΔ, não «todo o comércio».

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Cash-machine fees in Greece now have a ceiling written into law. Article 48 of ν.5167/2024, amended on 25.07.2025 and in force since 11.08.2025, removes the commission on withdrawals from the issuing bank's own network, sets the fee at zero in a municipal community served by a single ATM, and caps at 1,50 euros per withdrawal what an independent operator may charge. The practical effect for a small island: the traveller is not at the mercy of whatever figure the machine announces.
fatosDatados.fonte: ACHADO NOVO E ÚTIL PARA ILHA — taxa de saque. O art. 48 do ν.5167/2024, alterado em 25.07.2025 e vigente desde 11.08.2025: elimina comissão em saque na rede do próprio banco emissor, zera a tarifa em comunidade municipal onde opera um ÚNICO ATM, e fixa teto nacional de €1,50 por saque cobrado por operador independente. Isso muda o conselho prático: o aluno em ilha pequena não está à mercê da taxa que a máquina anunciar.

steps.pt: Your first hour is four counters and four small questions. In Greece they all open the same way.
Here is the frame: έχετε, and then the thing. Do you have — and then whatever you happen to need.
Good morning, do you have a map?

steps.promptPt: At the information desk, paper survives a flat battery and yours is nearly flat. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Good morning, do you have a map?
Good morning! Yes, here you are.
Notice what the frame asks: not whether the thing exists somewhere, but whether this person has it.

steps.promptPt: At the phone shop by baggage reclaim, you want a local number for the week. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a card for the phone?
Καλημέρα comes first, every single time. Arriving with the request and no greeting is entering without knocking.

steps.promptPt: Back at the phone shop: your battery is at four percent and everything you own is in the hold bag. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a charger?
The thing after the frame arrives as one block. Learn έχετε χάρτη whole and never take it apart.

steps.promptPt: At the information desk again: the room is not ready until three and you are carrying everything. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have luggage storage?

steps.promptPt: The kiosk by the exit sells travel, and the machines have a long queue in front of them. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have metro tickets?
The frame does not care what the thing is. A map, a charger, tickets, water, coins, a toilet.

steps.promptPt: Still at the kiosk: the luggage trolley takes coins only and the machine gave you a twenty. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have small change?

steps.es: Όχι εδώ, αλλά έχει στο περίπτερο απέναντι.
steps.pt: Not here, but there is some at the kiosk opposite.
steps.tts: Όχι εδώ, αλλά έχει στο περίπτερο απέναντι.
steps.acao: Stay for the second half — the no arrives with the address of the yes attached.

steps.pt: Card is owed to you at a long list of trades here, and the notice has to be visible at the door and the till.

steps.promptPt: You are about to hand over your last note at the kiosk and you would rather keep it. Check first. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you take card?
A no usually carries the address of the yes. Stay one beat past the first word.

steps.promptPt: At the airport café, before an hour on the metro in August. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have water?

steps.promptPt: Still at the airport café, before the train and the long ride into town. Ask. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a toilet?
Of course, at the back on the right.
Cash machines have a fee ceiling now, and where a small community has just one, the fee is zero.

steps.promptPt: They sorted you out in ten seconds. Close it the way people close things here. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you very much! Have a good day.

steps.es: Έχετε χάρτη; Έχετε φορτιστή; Έχετε ψιλά;
steps.pinyin: E-khe-te KHAR-ti. E-khe-te for-ti-STI. E-khe-te psi-LA
steps.pt: Shadow the same opening across three completely different counters.
steps.tts: Έχετε χάρτη; Έχετε φορτιστή; Έχετε ψιλά;

steps.pt: B06 done. One frame, four counters, and the whole first hour answered with έχετε and a noun.

aprofundar.titulo: One opening, nine things to ask for

secoes.corpo: Keep έχετε and put after it anything a person behind a counter could physically have. The opening never changes: it is already the polite plural, it is already a question once your voice lifts at the end, and nothing in it depends on who you are talking to. That is what makes it the cheapest frame in the course.

secoes.titulo: The thing after it comes as one block
secoes.corpo: Greek changes the ending of a noun according to its job in the sentence, and after έχετε that ending is fixed. You are not being asked to work anything out under pressure: έχετε χάρτη, έχετε φορτιστή, έχετε τουαλέτα are learned whole, the way you learned a phone number. The dictionary form of χάρτη is χάρτης, and you can ignore that fact entirely for the whole of this trip.

secoes.titulo: What they have, not what exists
secoes.corpo: English reaches for is there a…, and Greek has υπάρχει for exactly that. It is correct and it is the speech of someone who already lives there. At a counter the natural Greek question is about the person in front of you — what do you have — and that small shift is the difference between reading from a phrasebook and sounding like someone who has done this before.

secoes.titulo: Card, cash and the sign at the door
secoes.corpo: Greece obliges a great many trades to accept a card, not merely to own a terminal, and to say so visibly at the entrance and at the till. The duty attaches to the trade's activity code rather than to commerce in general, so it is not universal — but it covers far more ground than the equivalent in Italy or France, and street markets, food shops and kiosks were added to the list at the end of 2023. IRIS, the instant-payment system you will see advertised, is domestic: a foreign visitor normally cannot use it, and does not need to.

secoes.titulo: The no that carries an address
secoes.corpo: Όχι εδώ, αλλά… is the standard shape of a Greek no at a counter. Walking away on the first word leaves the useful half on the table — the kiosk opposite, the other terminal, the machine that does break a twenty.

permissao: You do not need a different sentence for each counter in that hall, and nobody there is grading your grammar. Καλημέρα, έχετε, the thing, and a rising tone is a complete request anywhere in the building — and you are allowed to use the identical three words at all four counters without varying them to sound better.
espelho: Anyone landing in an unfamiliar airport at home already runs this exact triage without naming it — signal, money, bags, somewhere to stand. The only new part is doing it in three words that never change.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You reach a till with a card and are told, flatly, that it is cash only.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Small places here simply do not take cards, and arguing would be rude and pointless.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Greek law obliges a long list of trades to accept card payment — the duty is to accept, not merely to have a terminal — and to display that fact visibly at the entrance and at the till. The list was widened at the end of 2023 to cover street markets, food retail and kiosks.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask before you order rather than after, and look at the door and the till on the way in. If the notice is there, the card is good; if you would rather not have the conversation, pay in cash and move on.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop treating card acceptance as a favour, and you find out at the moment when you still have a choice about where to spend.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: The legal criterion is the trade's activity code, not commerce in general, so this is not a claim that every business in Greece must take a card. And IRIS, which you will see advertised alongside cards, is a domestic system a foreign visitor normally cannot use.

fichasCulturais.sinal: The cash machine on a small island announces a fee before it dispenses, and you accept it because there is no other machine to walk to.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: One machine on the island means the machine sets the price, and there is nothing to be done about it.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Since August 2025 the fee has a legal ceiling. Withdrawals inside your own issuing bank's network carry no commission, an independent operator may charge at most one euro fifty per withdrawal, and in a municipal community served by a single machine the fee is zero.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Read the fee screen instead of clicking through it, and take out a sensible amount in one withdrawal rather than several small ones.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: A fee you did not expect becomes a number you can check, and you stop planning your cash around a charge that may not be lawful.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: It says nothing about whether there is a machine at all. Bank branch numbers on the islands have fallen sharply, the figures circulating come from press reports rather than a per-island series, and carrying some cash to a small island stays a sensible precaution rather than a statistic.
